newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down on arb, India.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down on arb, India.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps fell late afternoon on Monday as the market discounted the volume India intends to take in its second tender amid growing anxiety over talks of several arbitrage cargoes from Europe.
"The market is discounting India's second tender and this is pushing prices down," one trader said.
March gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.95/$25.05 per barrel, down from Friday's $25.20/$25.30, brokers said.
The market traded earlier in the day at $25.05, $25.00 and $24.95 per barrel, they said.
India awarded 570,000 tonnes of 1.0 percent gas oil in its first tender, less than the 700,000 tonnes that was widely expected by traders on Friday.
But to make up for the low award, India issued a second April import tender amounting to 270,000 tonnes, which would bring the total purchase up to 840,000 tonnes.
Traders said India is not expected to buy the full 270,000-tonnes that it tendered for.
Market jitters were also attributed to persistent talks of arbitrage cargoes headed to the region with about two 45,000-tonne cargoes said fixed for shipment to India from the Mediterranean.
Two other traders are believed to have fixed vessels for the shipment of cargoes from Northwest Europe to the region, sources said.
The cargoes, one for 220,000-tonne and the other 80,000-tonne, are expected into the region in April but traders involved in the deal deny such exports.
Jet fuel remains under selling pressure with some traders saying the market was over valued. March regrade was last quoted at $1.50/$1.80 per barrel, down 10 cents from Friday.
Fuel oil swaps were down in line with weaker crude with March last quoted at $100.00/$101.00 per tonne, down $2.00 from Friday. The market traded earlier in the day at $101.00 and $100.50.
